ceremony.intro: The tea ceremony (lễ gia tiên) is at one of the couple's homes, not at the reception hall. Families do this differently. Treat the order below as a draft to confirm with both families, not as a rule.

order.title: House is ready
order.detail: Altar, backdrop, tea set, trays, and extra chairs are in place before anyone arrives. To confirm who is in charge of the room.

order.title: Groom's family arrives
order.detail: If you also do lễ rước dâu, this is the visit to the bride's house. To confirm whether you want that procession or only the tea at one home.

order.title: Trays come in
order.detail: Carriers and receivers walk the mâm quả in. With 4 and 4 in the wedding party, 5 trays needs one extra person per side and 7 trays needs three.

order.title: Greeting and bows
order.detail: The couple greets both families and bows at the ancestor altar. The exact number of bows is a family decision.

order.title: Tea for the elders
order.detail: The couple serves tea. Elders may speak and give lì xì. To confirm the order of elders with both families.

order.title: Photos, then a break
order.detail: Pictures at the house, then time to eat, rest, and change before the reception.

trays.note: Traditional. To confirm that both families still want this tray.
For serving the elders, and often a tray of its own.
Common. Skip it if a family prefers not to.
The fruit-tray photo in this section is a Tết arrangement, only a visual starting point.
To confirm flavors and whether anything is made at home.
Often included and often the awkward one to transport. To confirm.

setup.item: Extra chairs and tables for family
Tent or shade, only if the yard needs it
Cars between the house and the reception

ceremony.morning: A working guess, to confirm: start preparing the room by 7:30, family in place around 8:30, tea finished before noon, then a long break before an evening reception. No venue rental is budgeted for this house.
